summary: Responsive romantic Valentine web page that starts with a friendly 404 "Page Not Found" screen and Refresh button, then transitions to a "Will you be my Valentine Oishi?" YES/NO prompt with animated interactions (YES reveals an agreement message with updated bullet list: Unlimited cuddles, Lifetime supply of milk, Unlimited sex, Daily minimum 1 nudes; hides buttons after 1s; triggers 5s confetti; NO jumps randomly, changes gradient colors, and updates an emoji after two clicks), implemented via reveal/hide without replacing the full container.
architectural_notes: Implement as a self-contained static HTML page with embedded CSS/JS for easy local use on iPad Chrome.
Avoid replacing the entire container; implement screen changes by showing/hiding existing elements with smooth transitions.

existing_features.title: Create a single-purpose Valentine prompt page that asks the user: “Will you be my Valentine?” and presents exactly two prominent options: “Yes” and “No”.
Implement an interaction where hovering over the “No” option causes it to move away so it cannot be clicked, effectively preventing selection of “No”.
When the user clicks “Yes”, replace the prompt with a success state that displays a meme image and the exact text: “Good choice”.
Apply a romantic theme using a pink-and-white color scheme with cohesive typography, spacing, and decorative styling (e.g., subtle hearts or soft gradients) across the entire page.
Ensure the page is fully interactive and works well in Chrome on iPad (responsive layout, touch-friendly button sizing, and pointer interactions that degrade gracefully on touch devices).
Add the generated images as static frontend assets and render them directly from the frontend (do not serve images through the backend).

Update the success-state headline text (the <h1> in the accepted/"Yes" state) to exactly: "Good Choice Putuu". Apply this change only to the selected element at XPath /html[1]/body[1]/div[1]/div[1]/div[2]/div[1]/h1[1] (i.e., the success-state <h1> currently rendering "Good choice" in frontend/src/App.tsx).

Add an initial 404-style screen that is shown on first load, displaying the friendly headline text "Page Not Found" and a centered "Refresh" button; clicking "Refresh" must smoothly transition to the Valentine invitation screen without re-mounting/replacing the entire root container.
Update the Valentine invitation screen content to ask exactly: "Will you be my Valentine Oishi?" and render two centered buttons labeled exactly "YES" and "NO".

Implement the YES click flow: when "YES" is clicked, immediately reveal the agreement message block with the exact text and bullet list provided by the user; after 1 second, smoothly hide both YES and NO buttons; also trigger a confetti effect that runs for 5 seconds and then disappears.

Implement the NO click behavior: clicking "NO" (not hover) makes the NO button jump to random positions on the screen area, changes the soft gradient background to different colors each time, and continues this behavior indefinitely until "YES" is clicked or the page is reloaded.

Add a visible heartbreak emoji indicator (💔) associated with the NO interaction and update it to 😭 after the user has clicked "NO" exactly two times; the emoji must remain 😭 for subsequent NO clicks until the page is reloaded.

Ensure styling and motion meet the design requirements: keep a soft gradient background, rounded edges, subtle shadows, one consistent stylish font across all text, and smooth, natural transitions between the 404 screen and Valentine screen and between interaction states (message reveal, button hide, NO jumps).

Update the YES-click agreement message content shown in the Valentine invitation screen (in frontend/src/App.tsx) so it displays exactly this headline and bullet list (and no additional trailing sentence):

Headline (exact text):
"By clicking YES you agree to:"

Bullets (exact text, in this order):
- "Unlimited cuddles"
- "Lifetime supply of milk"
- "Unlimited sex"
- "Daily minimum 1 nudes"
